trust.title: Trust Local Domains
trust.description: Browsers open your local domains without a warning once this computer trusts Teitunnel's certificate authority.
trust.step1: Teitunnel makes its own certificate authority. Its private key stays in your keychain.
trust.step1@windows: Teitunnel makes its own certificate authority. Its private key stays in Credential Manager.
trust.step1@linux: Teitunnel makes its own certificate authority. Its private key stays in your keyring.
trust.step2: It's added to your login keychain as trusted. macOS asks for your password.
trust.step2@windows: It's added to your trusted certificates. Windows asks you to confirm.
trust.step2@linux: It's added to Chrome's and Firefox's certificate lists. The system's list needs an administrator.
trust.step3: Each local domain gets a short-lived certificate that renews by itself.
trust.safety: The authority can only sign .localhost, .test and .local names and local addresses, so even a stolen key couldn't impersonate a real website.
trust.browsers: Also add it to Chrome's and Firefox's own certificate lists (uses NSS tools when installed)
trust.firefoxDetail: Firefox trusts the system's certificates by default since version 120; this turns that back on in profiles where it was switched off.
trust.adminDetail: Only an administrator can change the system's certificate list. Run these commands in a terminal, or let Teitunnel ask for your password.
trust.stopDetail: Browsers warn about every local domain again until you trust it again.
